how: `a` takes its default 5 and `b` its default 0, both `u16`, so `core.remainder` of 5 by 0 is a fault: by 0 both `core.quotient` and `core.remainder` are a fault, and `core.remainder` has no `err` (spec 8.2, A.1 `Bits and integer division`). The fault is `LC8008`, the code of a value that its operation cannot take where no `err` can say it (spec 8.2, Q-25; cli.md 6.6), at the node `y`, the line `y = core.remainder(a, b)`, as in `fault-LC8008-overflow`. No loop is around it; no output (spec 8.2, commands.md 7), no resource. The simulated clock stays at 0 ms: nothing waits before the fault (spec 8).
